svg.title: Base-Case Gross Receipts to $143,500 Owner Profit
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-03-base-owner-profit-bridge; chart type: waterfall; title: Base-Case Gross Receipts to $143,500 Owner Profit; subtitle: $1,025,000 gross receipts; 35% retained spread; 14.0% gross-basis margin.; chapter number: 3; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Formula v2.0 endpoints are canonical; the three expense buckets are an illustrative allocation. Opening and closing bars are totals; intermediate bars are signed deductions. Conservative gross $250,000 less 65% basis leaves $87,500 retained contribution and $20,000 owner profit: 8% gross-basis margin and 22.86% retained margin. Base retained contribution is $358,750 with 40.0% retained margin. Scaled gross $1,800,000 leaves $630,000 retained contribution and $360,000 profit: 20% gross-basis margin and 57.14% retained margin. The retained_share=0.35 convention is the scorecard's net presentation; actual ASC 606 principal-versus-agent analysis determines recognized revenue for each contract.; caption: $1,025,000 - $666,250 - $61,500 - $96,000 - $57,750 = $143,500. Gross reimbursements and resale proceeds are not interchangeable with retained operator revenue.; stages: label: Gross receipts; value: $1,025,000 annual scorecard gross receipts; numeric value: 1025000.0; detail: Aggregate buying-group reimbursements, card-rebate yields and ticket resale proceeds once each. Exclude unrelated merchant sales and card borrowing from this gross total.; label: Merchandise and ticket basis; value: Subtract $666,250 of direct acquisition basis; numeric value: -666250.0; detail: Deduct landed merchandise and face-value ticket basis at 65% of aggregate gross receipts. Remaining modeled retained contribution equals $358,750, or 35%.; label: Transaction and distribution costs; value: Subtract $61,500 of variable execution costs; numeric value: -61500.0; detail: Allocate 6.0% of gross receipts to exchange commissions, payment charges and selling-side fulfillment costs. Exclude costs already capitalized within landed acquisition basis.; label: Recurring pod operating costs; value: Subtract $96,000 of annual operating costs; numeric value: -96000.0; detail: Allocate $8,000 monthly to contractors, software, bookkeeping, business insurance and administration. This fits the $1,500–$9,000 monthly range; owner draws are distributions.; label: Loss and carrying costs; value: Subtract $57,750 of modeled residual costs; numeric value: -57750.0; detail: Allocate realized markdowns, credit losses, rebate reversals and borrowing costs without duplicating acquisition basis or exchange fees; residual costs equal this scenario balance.; label: Annual owner net profit; value: $143,500 remaining after all modeled costs; numeric value: 143500.0; detail: Closing total equals 14.0% of $1,025,000 gross receipts and 40.0% of $358,750 retained contribution. It is the owner-profit endpoint, not an additional cash receipt.

text.title: Base-Case Gross Receipts to $143,500 Owner Profit
text.tspan: Base-Case Gross Receipts to $143,500 Owner Profit

rect.title: label: Gross receipts; value: $1,025,000 annual scorecard gross receipts; numeric value: 1025000.0; detail: Aggregate buying-group reimbursements, card-rebate yields and ticket resale proceeds once each. Exclude unrelated merchant sales and card borrowing from this gross total.

label: Merchandise and ticket basis; value: Subtract $666,250 of direct acquisition basis; numeric value: -666250.0; detail: Deduct landed merchandise and face-value ticket basis at 65% of aggregate gross receipts. Remaining modeled retained contribution equals $358,750, or 35%.

label: Transaction and distribution costs; value: Subtract $61,500 of variable execution costs; numeric value: -61500.0; detail: Allocate 6.0% of gross receipts to exchange commissions, payment charges and selling-side fulfillment costs. Exclude costs already capitalized within landed acquisition basis.

label: Recurring pod operating costs; value: Subtract $96,000 of annual operating costs; numeric value: -96000.0; detail: Allocate $8,000 monthly to contractors, software, bookkeeping, business insurance and administration. This fits the $1,500–$9,000 monthly range; owner draws are distributions.

label: Loss and carrying costs; value: Subtract $57,750 of modeled residual costs; numeric value: -57750.0; detail: Allocate realized markdowns, credit losses, rebate reversals and borrowing costs without duplicating acquisition basis or exchange fees; residual costs equal this scenario balance.

label: Annual owner net profit; value: $143,500 remaining after all modeled costs; numeric value: 143500.0; detail: Closing total equals 14.0% of $1,025,000 gross receipts and 40.0% of $358,750 retained contribution. It is the owner-profit endpoint, not an additional cash receipt.

text.title: Assumptions: Formula v2.0 endpoints are canonical; the three expense buckets are an illustrative allocation. Opening and closing bars are totals; intermediate bars are signed deductions. Conservative gross $250,000 less 65% basis leaves $87,500 retained contribution and $20,000 owner profit: 8% gross-basis margin and 22.86% retained margin. Base retained contribution is $358,750 with 40.0% retained margin. Scaled gross $1,800,000 leaves $630,000 retained contribution and $360,000 profit: 20% gross-basis margin and 57.14% retained margin. The retained_share=0.35 convention is the scorecard's net presentation; actual ASC 606 principal-versus-agent analysis determines recognized revenue for each contract.
